text: Given a mocked KPN disturbance-check response with one open broadband disturbance, When kpn_check_disturbance is called, Then has_disturbance is true and disturbances contains that entry with service/state/description.
Given a mocked KPN disturbance-check response with all four arrays empty, When kpn_check_disturbance is called, Then the tool returns has_disturbance=false, disturbances=[] (not an error envelope).

Given a mocked KPN speed-check response with FIBER at 500/500 Mbps, When kpn_check_internet_speed is called, Then technologies includes FIBER with download/upload=500 and max_download_mbps/max_upload_mbps=500.

Given a real Dutch address and real KPN credentials, When kpn_check_internet_speed is called against KPN's live API on INT, Then the response shape matches TC3's mocked assumption (no KeyError/ValidationError, field names line up).
steps: Obtain a real KPN sandbox/trial client id + secret (needs a real vendor account)
Call kpn_check_internet_speed via the deployed INT service with Header X-Kpn-Client-Id / X-Kpn-Client-Secret and a known real Dutch address
Compare the raw KPN response and the tool's parsed result against the shape assumed in TC3
expect: No deserialization error; field names (technologies[].name/download/upload, max_bandwidth.up/down) match what the code expects
evidence: needs a real vendor account — no KPN sandbox credentials available at design time; does not block development or INT publish per mcp-track.md 2.5

text: Given a mocked KPN SIM-swap response {latestSimChange: 2026-10-29T17:38:22.306Z}, When kpn_check_sim_swap is called, Then the tool result is {latest_sim_change: 2026-10-29T17:38:22.306Z}.
Given a mocked KPN 404 SIM_SWAP.UNKNOWN_PHONE_NUMBER response, When kpn_check_sim_swap is called, Then the tool returns the error envelope with code=not_found, retryable=false.

Given a POST /mcp request missing X-Kpn-Client-Secret, When it reaches the service, Then the response is 401 listing X-Kpn-Client-Secret as missing, and no outbound call to KPN (token exchange or API) was made.

Given two concurrent simulated requests with different client-id/secret pairs, When both call a tool at the same time, Then each request's ContextVar read returns only its own credentials and the token-cache lookups never cross tenants.

Given each documented KPN status/error code (400/401/403/404/409/429/500/503/504, plus a simulated connect timeout), When the corresponding tool call fails, Then the returned envelope's code and retryable match the mapping table in the tech design.
